newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: OSCE says delegation to go to Belgrade on Friday.
newsitem.headline: OSCE says delegation to go to Belgrade on Friday.

text.p: The Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe said on Thursday a high-level delegation would travel to Belgrade on Friday to investigate a contested local poll that has sparked weeks of mass protests in Serbia.
"We are leaving for Belgrade on Friday and most probably we'll return on Saturday evening or Sunday," OSCE spokeswoman Melissa Fleming told Reuters.

The OSCE was called in by President Slobodan Milosevic in response to a storm of criticism from abroad and four weeks of sustained street protests at home over the annulment of local polls in November.

The Zajedno (Together) coalition says it was robbed of victory in 15 of Serbia's main towns and cities, including the capital, as Milosevic's ruling Socialists had annulled the votes. It demands reinstatement of its triumphs.

A Western diplomatic source in Vienna told Reuters that the head of the OSCE delegation, former Spanish prime minister Felipe Gonzalez, would "definitely" see Milosevic as well as the leaders of the Zajedno coalition.
Fleming declined to comment on the agenda of the delegation, saying the timetable was still being "hammered out".
